summary: Defines a MIB module for managing World Wide Web services, with objects that describe web servers and their activity.

eli5.summary: This is a set of standard dials and counters for web servers, such as how busy they are, readable by any monitoring tool.

questions: what is the www service mib
how to monitor a web server with snmp
what is a document transfer protocol
subtitle: A standard SNMP MIB for watching web servers, proxies and clients without reading log files.

tldr.problem: Web services were typically monitored through log files, which becomes hard when one organization runs many of them.
tldr.mechanism: The WWW Service MIB defines SNMP objects for service information, protocol statistics and document statistics. It is written against an abstract document transfer protocol, mapped to HTTP and FTP.
tldr.outcome: Operators can monitor heterogeneous web services with one set of objects, for short-term problem detection and troubleshooting. It does not cover accounting, hit metering or configuration.

today: RFC 2594 is a Proposed Standard from May 1999. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
This memo defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module for managing World Wide Web services. It extends the application management framework of the System Application MIB (SYSAPPL-MIB, RFC 2287) and the Application Management MIB (RFC 2564), but is self-contained and can be used without implementing either.

The goal is a standard set of objects for integrated performance and fault management across a mix of web services. The objects are meant for short-term operational uses such as problem detection and troubleshooting. Accounting and hit metering are explicitly out of scope, and so is configuration of web services, because server software was an open market with no consensus on a common way to configure it. An implementation must also be possible without a heavy CPU or memory burden on the web server.
sections.eli5: Instead of digging through diaries (log files) to see how a web server is doing, this gives every server the same set of gauges. It is for spotting trouble, not for billing.

sections.title: The SNMP Framework It Builds On
sections.content:
The MIB follows the SNMP Management Framework: an architecture, a Structure of Management Information (SMI) for describing objects, message protocols for SNMPv1, SNMPv2c and SNMPv3, protocol operations, and a set of fundamental applications plus view-based access control. Managed objects are accessed through a virtual information store called the MIB.

This module is written in SMIv2. A SMIv1 version can be produced by translation, and the result must be semantically equivalent, except where objects are omitted because no translation is possible (use of Counter64).
sections.eli5: SNMP is a common language that monitoring programs use to ask devices questions. This document just adds a new list of questions that web servers can answer.

sections.title: Services and the Abstract Document Transfer Protocol
sections.content:
The MIB is organized around WWW services: sets of actions that can be invoked on a document, provided or used by a client, a server or a proxy. It separates incoming from outgoing requests and responses, so one set of objects can give statistics for clients, servers and proxies. This is a service-oriented view, in contrast to the process-oriented view of the Application MIBs. A caching proxy's hit/miss ratio is not an object, but can be derived from the request and response counters.

To stay independent of any one protocol, the MIB assumes an abstract Document Transfer Protocol (DTP) that works in request/response style. Every request has a request type (an OCTET STRING), every response has a status code (an INTEGER), and a protocol may send several responses to one request, each counted separately. For document statistics, the primary response, the one saying whether the request succeeded, is used.
sections.eli5: The MIB pretends every web-like protocol works the same way: someone asks, someone answers, and the answer has a status number. That lets one set of gauges work for many protocols.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The objects fall into three groups.

  • Service information: one table describing all WWW services the SNMP agent manages, including those in virtual domains of a host. It holds administrative data such as a contact person and network data such as the transfer protocol.
  • Protocol statistics: five tables. wwwSummaryTable gives a quick overview of traffic, and wwwRequestInTable, wwwRequestOutTable, wwwResponseInTable and wwwResponseOutTable count each request or response type separately.
  • Document statistics: details of the last N attempts on documents, Top N documents by number of actions, Top N documents by content bytes transferred, and summary statistics over a time interval.

Top N statistics are collected in buckets filled over a configurable time interval. When an interval passes, a new wwwDocBucketTable entry is created, the Top N entries are computed, and if the bucket count exceeds wwwDocCtrlBuckets the oldest bucket and its entries are deleted. Sizes are controlled through wwwDocCtrlTable objects such as wwwDocCtrlLastNSize and wwwDocCtrlTopNSize, and wwwDocCtrlLastNLock lets a manager lock the fast-changing last-N table to read a consistent snapshot.
sections.eli5: There are three clipboards. One lists the web services. One counts requests and answers. One tracks which pages were visited most, in time-boxed batches, and old batches get thrown away.

sections.title: The MIB Definitions
sections.content:
The module is named wwwMIB and sits at { mib-2 65 }. Its first revision is dated 9902251400Z and was published as this RFC. It defines textual conventions that tie the objects to the abstract DTP:

  • WwwRequestType: an OCTET STRING of 1 to 40 octets naming the request type.
  • WwwResponseType: an Integer32 from 0 to 2147483647.
  • WwwOperStatus: the state of a service, one of down(1), running(2), halted(3), congested(4) or restarting(5).
  • WwwDocName: the server-relative name of a document, up to 255 octets, so a URL such as http://www.x.org/standards/search/search.cgi?string=test resolves to /standards/search/search.cgi.

The service table's index, wwwServiceIndex, reuses the Application MIB's applSrvIndex where an applicable instance exists. The full table and group definitions are in section 6 of the RFC and are not walked through object by object here.
sections.eli5: This part is the official list of gauge names and what values they can show. For example, a service can be down, running, halted, congested or restarting.

sections.title: Mappings to HTTP and FTP
sections.content:
Each mapping must define the identifier of the transfer protocol and how requests and responses are recognized.

For HTTP, a message whose start line is a Request-Line is a DTP request, and one with a Status-Line is a response. WwwRequestType is the method token and WwwResponseType is the Status-Code. HTTP usually runs over TCP on well-known port 80, so the default wwwServiceProtocol is { applTCPProtoID 80 }.

For FTP, every command is a request and every reply is a response. WwwRequestType is the FTP command token and WwwResponseType is the three-digit reply code. A single command can bring several replies, and multi-line replies with the same code count as one response. The default protocol is { applTCPProtoID 21 }, the control connection port. The text says further mappings, for example NNTP or WebNFS, might be defined later.
sections.eli5: For web pages, the request type is the action word like GET and the answer type is the status number. For file transfer the same idea applies with commands and reply codes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects are read-write, and unprotected writes can harm network operation. Several objects are also sensitive. The document statistics include the names of documents targeted by protocol operations, which reveals access statistics. Protocol statistics are less sensitive but still reveal usage and quality, so sites are advised to configure MIB views so that a user sees only the services they manage. The service and summary groups reveal the existence of services, which may matter for private ones.

SNMPv1 by itself is not secure, even on a secured network. The RFC recommends considering the SNMPv3 User-based Security Model (RFC 2574) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2575), and leaves proper SNMP configuration to the customer or user.
sections.eli5: The gauges can show which pages people read and which servers exist. So only the right people should be allowed to read them, and not just anyone should be able to turn the knobs.
